name: NotAction-Deny narrows a broad wildcard rule grant -> downgraded, NEVER blocked-by-deny
note: Allow s3:* on * with a same-policy Deny that uses NotAction:s3:GetObject on *. In real AWS that Deny denies every action EXCEPT s3:GetObject, so s3:GetObject stays ALLOWED - the wildcard grant is NARROWED, not fully blocked. A NotAction-Deny can never cover a broad/wildcard grant token (the NotAction-preserved action survives), so the allows(actiongroup:s3:*) edge must stay reachable (downgraded to conditionally-reachable), and the Deny is surfaced on its own separate denies edge. Rendering this identically to the genuinely-blocked control (Allow s3:* + Deny s3:*) would tell the user a still-reachable capability is definitively blocked - a false deny (threat-model T8). Regression fixture for the NotAction-Deny-vs-wildcard false-deny defect.
